title: Validity Periods, Recurring Courses and Variance Thresholds — Good Faith & Price Estimates
content:
Good Faith & Price Estimates carry a validity period counted in calendar days after the estimate is issued, a recurring-course limit, a reissue setting for recurring courses, and a variance threshold at which Patient Financial Services reviews actual liability against the estimate total.

| Estimate type | Validity (calendar days after issue within which the service must be performed for the quoted price to hold) | Maximum months one recurring-course estimate may cover | Any change in frequency or items of a recurring course requires a new version | Service scheduled after the validity period | Percent by which actual liability may exceed the estimate total before a variance review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Self-Pay Good Faith Estimate - Single Scheduled Service | 90 | 12 | no | new version at current prices | 10 |
| Self-Pay Good Faith Estimate - Procedure with Co-Providers | 90 | 12 | no | new version at current prices | 10 |
| Self-Pay Good Faith Estimate - Recurring Course of Care | 365 | 12 | yes | new version at current prices | 10 |
| Insured Patient Out-of-Pocket Estimate | 30 | 12 | no | new version at current prices | 15 |
| Riverbend Self-Pay Package Price - Imaging & Diagnostics | 90 | 12 | no | new version at current prices | 0 |
| Riverbend Self-Pay Package Price - Outpatient Surgery | 90 | 12 | no | new version at current prices | 0 |
| Riverbend Self-Pay Package Price - Maternity & Delivery | 300 | 12 | no | new version at current prices | 0 |

## Points of reading

- The validity period is counted in calendar days, not business days.
- A variance threshold of 0 on the three package types means any excess of actual liability over the estimate total is above the threshold.
- Example (hypothetical): on a type with a 10 percent threshold, an estimate total of 2000.00 corresponds to a liability 10 percent above it of 2200.00.
